draft.article: Thousands of South Florida community members gathered Saturday at the Miami-Dade Fair & Exposition grounds in Sweetwater for the annual Susan G. Komen More than Pink Walk. Officers responded just before 2 a.m. to the 500 block of Northwest 16th Street, where they found a man suffering from a gunshot wound to the groin. First responders on the scene administered emergency care until Miami-Dade Fire Rescue arrived. Crews then airlifted the victim to a nearby trauma hospital, where officials reported him to be in stable condition. Authorities said the person allegedly responsible for the shooting stayed at the location and was taken into custody. The police investigation remains ongoing.

headlines: ACRE COMMUNITIES PLANS 391 UNIT HOUSING TOWER IN MIAMI
NEW AFFORDABLE HOUSING HIGH RISE PROPOSED FOR MIAMI
COULD A NEW MIAMI HIGH RISE HOUSE A LOCAL FIRE STATION
draft.article: ACRE Communities is proposing a new 391-unit residential high-rise for Miami at 25 NW 6th Street and 604 NW 1st Avenue. Planned across 0.8 acres, the development could break ground in 2028 and finish by summer 2030. The project dedicates 156 residences to affordable housing for households earning up to 60 percent of the area median income, alongside 47 workforce units for those making up to 120 percent. Miami-Dade County recorded the median income at $87,200 as of 2025. Rather than retail shops, the ground floor could house a 13,000-square-foot fire station. The structure will also include 432 parking spaces for residential and public use.

DADE ADDED MIAMI TO ITS OFFICIAL NAME
THE ONLY COUNTY IN THE UNITED STATES WITH A HYPHENATED NAME

On November 13, 1997, Dade County officially changed its name to Miami-Dade County. This decision gave the region a permanent new designation and established a unique civic milestone.

Following that adjustment on November 13, 1997, Miami-Dade County earned a singular distinction across the entire nation. It is the only county in the United States with a hyphenated name. The addition of the hyphen created an official county title that remains completely unmatched anywhere else in the United States.
